from_quote: This Constitution, and the laws of the United States which shall be made in pursuance thereof, and all treaties made, or which shall be made, under the authority of the United States, shall be the supreme law of the land; and the judges in every state shall be bound thereby—any thing in the Constitution or laws of any state to the contrary notwithstanding
rationale: Lowndes reads "the 2d clause in the 6th article of the Constitution" and quotes it in full (the quotation passes through one word, "be", on which the scans disagree).
to_quote: This Constitution, and the Laws of the United States which shall be made in Pursuance thereof; and all Treaties made, or which shall be made, under the Authority of the United States, shall be the supreme Law of the Land; and the Judges in every State shall be bound thereby, any Thing in the Constitution or Laws of any State to the Contrary notwithstanding

from_quote: the President, with ten senators, if only ten attend, may make treaties to bind all the states
rationale: The Speaker answers an objection to "the article" by which the President with the Senate makes treaties; only the treaty-making clause fits.
to_quote: to make Treaties, provided two thirds of the Senators present concur

from_quote: a duty not exceeding ten dollars
rationale: Lowndes speaks of the twenty-year importation of negroes with a duty "not exceeding ten dollars", the wording of the importation clause.
to_quote: not exceeding ten dollars for each Person

from_quote: the President, with the concurrence of two thirds of the Senate, might make treaties
rationale: Rutledge describes the clause by which the President, with two thirds of the Senate, makes treaties, calling it "this article".
to_quote: to make Treaties, provided two thirds of the Senators present concur
